Compact code representing the country derived from the IBAN (e.g. "DE" for Germany). Use for filtering by country of the bank account.
The type of device through which the transaction was initiated (e.g., ANDROID, POS). Use to understand channel preferences and device risk.
The specific event in the payment processing flow (e.g., AUTH for authorisation, SETTLEMENT for final settlement). Use to monitor payment lifecycle milestones.
Total number of transactions, summed across the selected period.
The business date assigned to the payment transaction. Use for daily trend analysis and period comparisons.
City associated with the transaction, typically where the merchant or customer is located. Use for geographic analysis of payment activity.
Indicates whether the transaction failed (t) or succeeded (f). Use to isolate failed transactions and analyse failure rates.
Total revenue generated, summed across the selected period.
Unique identifier for the counterparty (e.g., merchant, recipient, sender) in the transaction. Use to track relationships between entities.
Segment classification of the customer initiating the transaction (e.g. RETAIL, CORPORATE). Use to compare behaviour across customer types.
Masked representation of the customer's account number (e.g. ****0000), preserving anonymity while allowing account-level analysis.
Total gross margin (revenue minus cost of goods sold), summed across the selected period. Indicates profitability before overheads.
Code of the marketing campaign tied to the transaction (e.g. CMP001). Use to evaluate campaign-driven transaction volumes.
Year-to-date base currency amount. Summed across the selected period, reflecting cumulative performance from the start of the year.

Total commission earned, summed across the selected period.
Timestamp when the transaction record was last updated. Use this for tracking recent changes and time-based record filtering.
Indicates whether the transaction was processed successfully (t) or not (f). Use to measure success rates and filter for completed transactions.
Total amount refunded, summed across the selected period.
Exact timestamp when the payment was posted to the system. Use for sequencing events and real-time analytics.
Flag indicating whether the transaction has been charged back: 't' for yes, 'f' for no. Use to separate chargeback transactions for analysis.
The pricing plan code assigned to the transaction (e.g. BUS, CORP, STD). Use to segment volumes and revenue by pricing tier.
Total discount applied to transactions. Summed across the selected period.
ISO currency code in which the transaction was settled (e.g. GBP, USD). Use to assess settlement currency exposure and FX requirements.
Classification of the customer (e.g., CORPORATE, INDIVIDUAL). Use to segment transactions by customer type.
Indicates whether the account type is currently active (true/false). Use to filter for active account types only.
Method by which the card information was entered for the transaction (e.g. contactless, chip, online). Use to analyse payment method usage and security patterns.
Unique identifier for the merchant involved in the transaction. Use to link to merchant details and analyse activity by merchant.
Average foreign exchange rate applied to transactions, averaged across the selected period.
Value of chargebacks raised against transactions. Summed across the selected period.
The risk decision applied to the transaction (APPROVE, DECLINE, ESCALATE, REVIEW). Use to monitor risk outcomes and approval rates.
The payment scheme or network that processed the transaction (e.g. VISA, SEPA, SWIFT). Use to analyse payment method mix and scheme performance.
Unique code identifying the counterparty bank (e.g. "BANK0263"). Use for filtering transactions by the counterparty bank.
Indicates whether the transaction was refunded (t) or not (f). Use to filter refunded transactions and analyse refund volumes.
Unique identifier for the payment transaction. Use for exact lookups and single-transaction analysis.
Month component derived from the business date, at a monthly granularity. Use for trend analysis across months.
Code representing the financial product associated with the transaction (e.g. "P001"). Use for filtering by product type.
Total monetary amount settled for the transactions, summed across the selected period.
Business category of the merchant involved in the transaction (e.g. Grocery, Transport). Use to analyse spending patterns by merchant type.
Compact code representing the account type (e.g., "CREDIT", "SAVINGS"). Use for exact filtering; use description for the full label in displays.
The calendar year extracted from the business date. Use for year-over-year trend analysis and annual reporting.
Unique identifier of the terminal where the transaction originated (e.g. TERM000006). Use to group transactions by terminal for operational analysis.
Indicates whether the payment was reversed (true/false). Use to analyse reversals, which undo previous transactions.
Code representing the region of the transaction (e.g. LON for London, NYC for New York). Use for regional performance comparisons and filtering.
The name of the transaction counterparty, used to identify the other party in the payment. Use this to group transactions by counterparty and analyse counterparty-specific activity.
ISO country code associated with the transaction (e.g. US, GB). Use to segment activity by country and support geographic reporting.
Monetary value of each payment transaction. Summed across the selected period to show total transaction value.
The final status of the payment (SUCCESS, FAILED, CANCELLED, REVERSED). Use to track completion rates and payment lifecycle analysis.
Timestamp when the transaction record was originally created. Use for tracking record creation time and age analysis.
Total tax applied to transactions, summed across the selected period.
The name of the product used for the transaction (e.g. Standard Payments, Merchant Services). Use to group and compare transaction activity by product line.
Flag indicating whether the transaction has been flagged as potentially fraudulent (true/false). Use to isolate suspicious transactions.
Flag indicating whether the transaction involved sanctioned parties (true/false). Use to identify and isolate sanctioned transactions.
Standard Merchant Category Code (MCC) indicating the type of merchant business (e.g., 5411 for grocery stores). Use to categorise spending by merchant type.
Human-readable label for the account type (e.g. "Credit", "Savings"). Use for display and grouping; use account_type_code for exact filtering.

Total number of days from onboarding start to first login, summed across onboardings. Tracks time to first engagement.

Service tier offered for the product (Enterprise, Standard, etc.).

Surrogate key for the received date dimension. Currently has no values populated, but intended for date joins.
Time window during which the warehouse operates (e.g., 06:00-18:00 or 24/7). Use for scheduling and throughput analysis.
The calendar day the record was last updated. Use for daily update tracking.
The monetary variance between the actual price and a reference price (e.g., standard cost), summed across records. Currently zero.
The functional type of warehouse (e.g., Bonded Warehouse, Returns Centre). Use to categorize storage facilities.
State or province code where the warehouse is located. Use for geographic distribution analysis.
Purchase order number associated with the invoice line. Use to relate invoices to procurement orders and filter by PO.
The price per unit of the item on the invoice line, averaged across selected records.
The email address used to contact the vendor. Use for communication and vendor management.
Indicates whether the product is classified as hazardous material (true/false). Use for safety and storage compliance.
The number of units ordered on the invoice line, summed across selected records.
Indicates whether the warehouse can store hazardous materials. Use to filter hazardous-storage locations.
Unique identifier for each invoice (e.g. 'INV-00000001'). Use for grouping and searching by invoice.
The calendar month part of the product's effective start date. Use for monthly breakdowns.
The difference between the quantity ordered and the quantity actually fulfilled or received. Summed to show total variance across line items.
Name of the warehouse or distribution centre (e.g., Dallas Cross-Dock). Use for site-level analysis and reporting.
The credit rating assigned to the vendor, reflecting its creditworthiness. Use to filter vendors by risk level and for supplier evaluation.
Percentage of the vendor's past deliveries that arrived on time. Use to evaluate vendor reliability and performance.
The calendar year when the order was placed. Use to analyse ordering trends by year.
Date the order was placed. Use to analyse ordering trends over time and compare periods.
Indicates whether invoices of this type require approval before payment. Use to filter for invoices needing additional review.
The total monetary amount of the invoice, summed across records. Currently not populated (zero).
The calendar day of the effective end date. Use for daily detail on when items or records ended their effective period.
The minimum order value (in currency) required by the vendor, summed across vendors to aggregate threshold amounts.
The net monetary amount for the line item, likely after discounts and before tax, summed across selected records.
International Commercial Terms (e.g. 'CIF', 'FOB') defining shipping responsibilities and costs. Use for logistics and cost analysis.
The monetary discount applied to the line item, summed across records. Currently always zero.
The calendar year the record was last updated. Use to understand update activity by year.
Indicates whether the warehouse has temperature-controlled storage. Use to identify facilities suitable for sensitive goods.
Compact code that uniquely identifies a vendor (e.g., VEND-0001). Use for exact filtering; use vendor_name for display and grouping.
The monetary threshold above which invoices of this type require approval, in base currency. Use to determine when approval rules are triggered.
Indicates whether the product has a limited shelf life (true/false). Use to manage expiry-sensitive inventory.
Geographic region of the vendor (e.g. 'APAC', 'LATAM'). Use for regional procurement analysis.
The ISO currency code for the monetary amount on the invoice line item. Use for multi-currency reporting.
The tax rate percentage applied to the line item, averaged across selected records.
Average margin percentage across the selected products. Computed as the arithmetic mean of individual product margin percentages.
Number of days from invoice date within which early payment discount applies. Use to assess discount eligibility.
Indicates whether invoices of this type impact inventory quantities. Use to distinguish inventory-affecting transactions.
Date when the product record becomes inactive or no longer valid. Current null values indicate no end date has been set.
Total number of loading docks across selected warehouses, summed when multiple warehouses are included.
The calendar year of the effective end date. Use for year-over-year analysis of when items, contracts, or records ceased to be active.
Email address of the user or system that created the invoice line item record. Use to audit data entry.
Total quantity of items received, summed across invoice line items.
Number of days the product can be stored before expiration. Use for inventory expiration analysis.
The remaining unpaid balance on the invoice, summed across records. Currently always zero.
Compact code identifying a payment terms record (e.g., PT-115N45). Use for exact filtering; use payment_terms_name for display.
Status of the invoice matching process, indicating if the invoice matched the PO and/or receipt (2-way, 3-way, No_Match). Use for exception monitoring.
Unique identifier for each invoice line item. Use for granular tracking of individual line-level charges and details within an invoice.
Surrogate key uniquely identifying a vendor. Use for linking to vendor details.
Stock keeping unit code that uniquely identifies a product. Use for exact product lookup and filtering.
Outcome of the quality inspection for the received items (e.g., Pass, Conditional_Accept). Use to monitor supplier quality.
The defect rate percentage of a vendor, averaged across selected vendors to show the overall defect rate.
The calendar year the record was created in the system. Use to analyse record creation trends by year.
The number of defective units on the line item, summed across records. Currently not populated (100% null).
The cost price per unit of the product. Summing adds up cost prices across products; not a typical aggregate.
Average lead time in days for the vendor to deliver orders. Use to analyse supplier performance and filter by typical delivery speed.
The business classification of the vendor (e.g., Distributor, Wholesaler). Use to segment vendors for sourcing analysis.
Average number of days required from placing a replenishment order to receiving the goods. Use for inventory planning and safety stock calculation.
More granular product grouping within a category (e.g., Accessories, Wellness). Use for detailed inventory analysis.
Indicates whether the line item is part of a return. Use to separate returns from sales for accurate netting.
The number of days between invoice date and payment date for this line item. Summed across records. Currently not populated (100% null).
The city where the warehouse is located. Use for geographic distribution analysis.
Surrogate key that uniquely identifies each invoice line item. Use for granular record-level identification.
The calendar day when goods were received. Use for precise daily receiving records.
Detailed explanation of the payment terms, such as discount and net due dates. Useful for clarifying the exact conditions.

Total tax amount applied to invoice lines, summed across selected records. Note that all values in the current data are zero.
The name of the product. Use for display and product-level analysis.
The minimum quantity that can be ordered for a product. Summing aggregates these thresholds across multiple products.
Total weight in kilograms, summed across the selected products or invoice lines.
The calendar day the record was created. Use for daily detail on record creation.
Sum of discount percentages applied to invoice lines. For the average discount rate, use an average aggregation instead.
The calendar day a payment was made. Use for daily payment detail.
The current payment status of the invoice line item (e.g., Disputed, Written Off). Use for accounts receivable monitoring.
Average exchange rate used to convert the invoice line amount into US dollars, averaged across the selected records.
The total monetary amount for the invoice line item, including item cost, adjustments, and possibly tax, summed across selected records.
The calendar day of the promised delivery date. Use for daily detail on when deliveries were promised.
The date when payment was made. Currently not populated, but intended to capture actual payment dates.
Human-readable label for the payment terms (e.g., 1.5/15 Net 45). Use for display and grouping; use payment_terms_id for exact filtering.
Postal code of the warehouse address. Use for location-based analysis.
Total volume in cubic meters, summed across selected products or invoice lines.
Number of individual units per pack of the product. Use to compare pack configurations.
Supplier performance rating category (e.g. 'A', 'B', 'C'). Use for vendor evaluation and sourcing decisions.
ISO country code where the warehouse is located (e.g. "AE", "US"). Use to filter or group inventory and sourcing data by country.
The shipping cost associated with the invoice line item, summed across selected records.
The calendar month of the effective end date. Use to analyse effective end trends by month.
The currency in which the vendor is paid. Use for currency-specific financial analysis.
Indicates whether the product is currently active in the inventory catalogue. (All products in this dataset are active.)
Surrogate key uniquely identifying a warehouse. Use for linking to warehouse details.
Total days to deliver, summed across invoice lines. This measure is currently null for all rows, indicating the data has not been populated yet.
The sequential line number of the item within the invoice. Summing is atypical; normally used for sorting or grouping.
The calendar month a payment was made. Use for monthly payment trend analysis.
The partnership tier or status of the vendor (e.g., Approved, Trial). Use to distinguish vendor relationships.
The calendar year when goods were received. Use to track year-over-year receiving volumes.
The calendar month the record was created. Use for monthly creation analysis.
Date the vendor promised to deliver the goods. Use for tracking on-time performance and delivery trends.
Total quantity of items returned, summed across invoice lines. All values are currently zero, meaning no returns are recorded.
Reason for product return, if applicable (e.g. 'Damaged', 'Wrong_Item'). Use for returns analysis; nulls indicate no return.
Sum of retail prices across products, representing total potential revenue value at list price.
The calendar year an order or transaction was approved. Use to analyse approval timelines by year.
The timestamp when the record was last updated. With a single value, suggests the dataset is a snapshot.
High-level group the product belongs to (e.g., Automotive, Health). Use for broad inventory segmentation and reporting.
Surrogate key uniquely identifying payment terms applied to the invoice. Use for linking to payment terms details.
Name of the warehouse manager. Use to group or filter warehouse activity by responsible person.
Indicates whether the line item is a Credit (return/adjustment) or Debit (charge). Use to separate inflows from outflows.
The calendar day when the order was placed. Use for precise daily order tracking.
Two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) where the product originates. Use to analyse by country of supply.
Category of the purchase invoice or order type (e.g., Blanket PO Release, Urgent Purchase Order). Use to segment procurement activities.
Compact code identifying the warehouse (e.g. "WH-001"). Use for exact filtering by warehouse.
The calendar year part of the product's effective start date. Use for yearly product analysis.
Flag indicating whether this product record is the currently active version. All records are true, meaning only current products are in this dataset.
Internal surrogate key uniquely identifying a product record. Primarily used for technical joins; for business filtering, use product_id.
The calendar year of the promised delivery date. Use to analyse delivery promises by year.
Human-readable name of the vendor (e.g., Antwerp Diamond Trading Co). Use for display and grouping; use vendor_id for exact filtering.
Number of years the supplier has been in business relationship with the company. Use for tenure-based analysis.
The date when the invoice line item was approved. Use to analyze approval cycle times.
The calendar day part of the product's effective start date. Use for daily granularity.
The timestamp when the record was created. With a single value, it indicates a static dataset loaded at that time.
Sum of early payment discount percentages from payment terms. Use with caution; for the typical discount rate, consider average aggregation.
ABC classification of the product based on value/importance (A = high value, B = medium, C = low). Use for inventory prioritisation and cycle counting.
The calendar day an order or transaction was approved. Use for daily approval tracking.
Business code that uniquely identifies the product (e.g., ITEM-00001). Use for exact filtering and cross-referencing with other systems.
Surrogate date key linked to the invoice date. Use to join to a date dimension for time-based attributes like year, quarter, or month.
Surrogate key representing the date when the invoice payment is due. Use for time-based analysis by due date.
Maximum storage capacity of the warehouse, expressed in some unit (likely pallet or bin equivalents). Use for capacity planning.
The unit in which the product is measured (e.g., Each). All products in this dataset use 'Each'.
The total square footage of the warehouse facility, summed to show aggregate floor space across selected warehouses.
Annual spend band of the vendor, e.g. "1M-5M" or "<50K". Use to group vendors by their yearly procurement spending tier.
Indicates whether a quality inspection was performed on the received items (true/false). Use to filter or analyse inspection rates.
The calendar month when goods were received. Use for monthly receiving analysis.
The calendar year a payment was made. Use for year-over-year payment analysis.
The date from which this product definition is effective. With a single value, indicates a single version of product data.
The calendar month the record was last updated. Use for monthly update pattern analysis.
Categorises invoices by type (e.g., purchase, sales, credit). Use to filter or group records by the type of invoice.
The calendar month an order or transaction was approved. Use for monthly approval volume analysis.
The calendar month when the order was placed. Use for monthly order analysis.
Email address of the person who approved the invoice. Use to filter or group by approver.
Brand name under which the product is sold. Use for grouping and analysing performance by brand.
